s.t: Ruby Turner's 1985 cover, a duet with Jonathan Butler produced by Billy Ocean, reached number three in New Zealand but only number 30 in the UK.
s.src: Women Hold Up Half the Sky – Wikipedia (with the song article)
s.q: a cover of The Staple Singers song featuring Jonathan Butler; produced by Billy Ocean; reached No. 30 on the UK Singles Chart. Song article: Her version reached #30 in the UK, #29 in Ireland and number three in New Zealand.

f.t: Their founder Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples moved to Will Dockery's plantation near Drew, Mississippi, around 1923, where Charley Patton and Howlin' Wolf inspired him to take up guitar.
f.q: was inspired to take up guitar by local blues artists Charley Patton, Howlin’ Wolf, Dick Bankston, and Jim Holloway

f.t: Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples, their founder, paid fifty cents a week towards a Stella guitar at 14, then put it down for a dozen years while working in a slaughterhouse.
f.src: Forgotten Heroes: Pops Staples – Premier Guitar
f.q: By age 14 Staples was paying fifty cents a week towards a Stella he saw hanging in a store window. ... Staples put the guitar down for a dozen years while working in a slaughterhouse

f.t: Steve Cropper said of their founder Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples: ‘Everybody wanted to copy that tremolo sound, because he was one of the first guys to do it.’
f.src: Steve Cropper discusses Pops Staples' underrated contributions
f.q: Everybody wanted to copy that tremolo sound, because he was one of the first guys to do it.
